# Japan PR Guideline Check

> Free, unofficial checker for Japan's permanent residence guideline (永住許可に関するガイドライン), revised by the Immigration Services Agency (ISA) on 2026-10-01. Given a route and a filing date it applies the guideline version that matches the date, computes when the time-in-Japan requirement is met (old vs revised for spouse/child routes), and checks the objective factors: work-status years, longest period of stay incl. the 3-year transition, absences (6 months / 2.5 years), Japanese B1, school attendance, taxes and insurance; income and pension thresholds are not published. Rules as of 2026-10-18. Educational guide, not immigration or legal advice; never a verdict.

Site: https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app

## Key facts (official sources below)
- Which guideline applies depends on the date ISA RECEIVES the application (ISA notice 2026-10-01): filed up to 2026-03-31 → 2026-02-24 guideline; filed 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31 → 2026-02-24 guideline + only the income parts of the revision (2(4)(2) household income above the Japanese average for the household size, 2(5)(7) not a public burden); filed from 2027-04-01 → 2026-10-01 revised guideline in full.
- Spouse of a Japanese national / PR / SPR: 3+ years of substantive marriage and 1+ year in Japan (filed up to 2027-03-31) → 5+ years of marriage and 3+ years in Japan (from 2027-04-01). Biological / special-adopted child: 1+ year → 3+ years.
- General route: 10+ years continuous residence with 5+ years on a work or residence status. Technical Intern Training and Specified Skilled Worker (i) never count as work years; from 2027-04-01 also Employment for Skill Development, Intra-company Transferee and some Designated Activities.
- Longest period of stay: a 3-year period counts up to 2027-03-31; from 2027-04-01 only if held on 2027-03-31, the PR application is the first one filed from 2027-04-01, and the decision comes before that 3-year period expires.
- Absences (filed from 2027-04-01): in the 10 years before filing, one trip of 6+ months or 2 years 6 months+ abroad in total, without a reasonable reason, is generally assessed negatively. ISA publishes no day-count method (this tool: calendar 6 months; 913 days).
- New factors from 2027-04-01: Japanese at CEFR B1+ (exempt: HSP and family, 6+ years schooling in Japan, PR's child born in Japan with a B1 parent; method to be announced), understanding of Japan's rules (Living and Working Guidebook), projected pension vs 30 years of Employees' Pension (or assets), school-age children attending school.
- Income, pension and asset thresholds are NOT published (public-comment answers No. 17, 34). Spouses/children of Japanese/PR and recognized refugees are exempt from the independent-livelihood test.
- Fee: ¥200,000 for applications received from 2026-10-01 (was ¥10,000), paid only when granted.
- The separate "contribution to Japan" PR guideline is abolished on 2027-03-31. PR revocation rules (2024 Immigration Act amendment) take effect 2027-04-01.

## API (free, no key, CORS open)

### GET
GET https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app/api/check?route=spouse&applicationDate=2027-02-15&residenceSince=2025-09-01&marriageDate=2023-06-10&periodOfStay=3y
→ band "transition", timeRequirement.earliestDate "2026-09-01", filingWindow {oldRuleEarliest 2026-09-01, newRuleEarliest 2028-09-01, oldRuleDeadline 2027-03-31, canUseOldRule true}, summary "need_more_info" (taxes/insurance not given), checks[], keyDates[], fee, sources, disclaimer

### POST
POST https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app/api/check
{"route":"general","applicationDate":"2027-06-01","yearsInJapan":11,"workYears":6,"currentStatus":"intra_company_transferee","periodOfStay":"5y","trips":[{"depart":"2020-01-10","return":"2020-07-10"}],"japaneseB1":"yes"}
→ summary "objective_issue" (a 6-month trip; ICT years flagged for review)

Parameters: route (general | spouse | child | long_term_resident | refugee | hsp70 | hsp80 | special_hsp | contribution | special_zone_regional; required), applicationDate (YYYY-MM-DD, default today JST), residenceSince or yearsInJapan, workYears, marriageDate, qualifyingSince, currentStatus, periodOfStay (5y|3y|1y|6m|3m|unlimited|other), periodExpiry, firstPrApplication, trips (POST array or GET "depart_return,depart_return"), longestTripDays, totalAbsenceDays, japaneseB1, b1Exemption, schoolAgeChildren (none|all_in_school|not_in_school), taxesPaidOnTime, pensionInsurancePaidOnTime.
summary is one of objective_issue | need_more_info | no_objective_blocker. It is never an approval prediction.

### Other endpoints
- GET https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app/api/rules (all rules, both versions, sources)
- https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app/openapi.json
- https://japan-pr-check.vercel.app/.well-known/ai-plugin.json
- MCP: tool japan_permanent_residency_check on https://free-agent-tools.vercel.app/mcp

- https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/10_00279.html (Guideline revised 2026-10-01, full text)
- https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/content/001471577.pdf (Guideline revised 2026-10-01, PDF)
- https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/applications/procedures/eizyuu_00001.html (ISA PR page: which guideline applies by filing date, 2026-10-01 notice)
- https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/applications/resources/nyukan_nyukan50.html (Guideline revised 2026-02-24)
- https://public-comment.e-gov.go.jp/pcm/1040?CLASSNAME=PCM1040&id=315000140&Mode=1 (public-comment results)
- https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/01_00644.html (fees)

## Disclaimer
Educational guide, not immigration or legal advice. Permanent residence is discretionary; ISA decides and does not publish its income thresholds. Not affiliated with ISA or the Ministry of Justice.
